subunit: Interacts with PFN1. Interacts through its N-terminus with PRPF40A. Interacts with PQBP1. Interacts with SETD2. Interacts with SH3GLB1. Interacts with SYVN. Interacts with TPR; the interaction is inhibited by forms of Huntingtin with expanded polyglutamine stretch. Interacts with ZDHHC13 (via ANK repeats). Interacts with ZDHHC17 (via ANK repeats). Interacts with F8A1/F8A2/F8A3. Found in a complex with F8A1/F8A2/F8A3, HTT and RAB5A; mediates the recruitment of HTT by RAB5A

complexes.name: Huntingtin-HAP40 endosomal complex
complexes.function: The HTT-HAP40 complex plays several key biological roles, including maintaining protein stability, regulating intracellular transport, and modulating cellular homeostasis. The complex acts as a RAB5A (P20339) effector, regulating early endosome motility by recruiting kinesins-1 and -3 to facilitate anterograde motility along microtubules, thereby affecting intracellular cargo transport and membrane dynamics. Binding of F8A1 to HTT is thought to reduce the aggregation and toxicity of mutant HTT in Huntington’s disease, and to promote its proteasomal degradation via K48-linked ubiquitination.
complexes.properties: HTT HEAT repeats form a large solenoid-like structure at the N-terminal region of the protein and a more compact C-terminal region. The N-HEAT and C-HEAT regions are connected by a bridge domain, composed of repetitive alpha-helical structures with F8A1 sandwiched between these regions. F8A1 binds in a cleft and interacts with three HTT domains through hydrophobic and electrostatic interactions to stabilize the conformation of HTT, and in doing so, F8A1 plays a key role in regulating the conformation of HTT. However, both proteins are mutually dependent on maintaining stability. HTT typically adopts a globular helical structure, but polyglutamine expansion disrupts this conformation, potentially altering the orientation and dynamics of its intrinsically disordered regions.
